exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal delivery, caesarean section)
cohort: The study included over 300 puerperal women, with 149 having vaginal deliveries and 151 having caesarean sections.
finding: Overall, 31.6% of women experienced urogynaecological symptoms in the first week postpartum, which decreased to 7.3% by 6 weeks postpartum.
mod_finding: There were no significant differences in the prevalence of various urogynaecological symptoms between women who had a vaginal delivery and those who had a caesarean section.
birth_weight: Mean 2.62 kg (vaginal delivery group) vs. 2.75 kg (caesarean section group)
gest_age: Mean 37.5 weeks (vaginal delivery group) vs. 38.4 weeks (caesarean section group)
